claims.text: A tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy using low-activation alloying elements can serve as an improved structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components.
The proposed alloy would lower long-term activation relative to conventional tungsten.
The proposed alloy would mitigate irradiation-induced damage relative to conventional tungsten.
Tungsten has a high melting temperature and low sputter or erosion rates, making it a leading plasma-facing-material candidate.
Tungsten develops helium-induced bubbles and related surface damage under relevant particle exposure.
Pure tungsten has problematic activation characteristics under irradiation.
Fusion divertor plasma-facing materials must operate at temperatures of at least 1000 K while exposed to high heat and intense neutron and particle irradiation.
High configurational entropy in the proposed alloy will produce a nanocrystalline microstructure containing coherent nanoprecipitates.
The nanocrystalline structure and coherent nanoprecipitates will promote uniform, stable grains under irradiation and thermal loading.
High configurational entropy reduces phase instability and irradiation-induced defect aggregation.
The intrinsic nanostructure and coherent precipitates enable effective dislocation motion.
The intrinsic nanostructure and coherent precipitates reduce helium-bubble nucleation.
Selecting low-activation alloying elements will minimize the production of long-lived radioactive isotopes.
Refractory high-entropy alloys can provide strong mechanical performance at elevated temperatures.
The tungsten-based HEA will exhibit reduced tritium retention relative to traditional tungsten.
The combined improvements in radiation tolerance, helium-bubble formation, tritium retention, and activation will enhance plasma-facing-component operational viability.
Adding certain elements to refractory high-entropy alloys can introduce brittle intermetallic phases.
Oxidation resistance is a potentially limiting property of refractory high-entropy alloys at high temperature.
Fabrication and control of the desired nanocrystalline, precipitate-containing microstructure are critical to realizing the proposed performance gains.
The optimal combination of low-activation refractory elements for the proposed tungsten-based HEA has not been established.
